device.name: USB flash drive with no asset tag (found in the parking lot)

checks.observation: None, while official PT Nusa Digital drives always carry an asset tag
Found by security in the parking lot this morning, no one has claimed it
Not checked yet: it has never been plugged into any computer

note.text: Security guard: Just plug it into the Workshop PC so we know whose it is. I will return it to the owner.

explanation: An unknown flash drive with a label that sparks curiosity, left in a parking lot, is classic bait for running malicious software as soon as it is plugged in. Do not plug it into any computer; hand it to the SOC team to be checked safely.
hints: This drive is not broken. Where did it come from, and why is its label so tempting?
An unknown item made to spark curiosity is a sign of an attack. Who is the expert at checking it?
